note: These are output-risk results. Per the preregistration none of them makes the runtime incompatible.

positiveTranscriptExact.explanation: Every character was recognised correctly and in order. The transcripts differ only by the two spaces: the model charset is the 94-character set (62 case-sensitive alphanumeric + 32 punctuation) and contains NO space character, so PARSeq structurally cannot emit a word boundary. This is a model property, not a recognition error.
positiveTranscriptExact.materialForBrand: A Brand value such as "La Fattoria" could at best come back as "lafattoria". Any future Brand benchmark must decide how to score word boundaries the model cannot represent.

blankTranscriptEmpty.explanation: The blank white image produced the two-character transcript "10".

blankProducedUnsupportedText.explanation: Text with no visual support was emitted from a blank image. Its per-character probabilities (0.313, 0.197) and sequence score (0.0208) are far below the positive case (all >0.96, score 0.256), which is suggestive but is not a calibrated abstention threshold.

modelHasNaturalAbstention.explanation: PARSeq is a fixed-length autoregressive sequence decoder with no null/abstain class. It returns a transcript for whatever it is given, including pure white. Any abstention would have to be imposed outside the model.

confidenceInterpretationKnown.explanation: Native probabilities are preserved in 0..1 and are internally ordered sensibly on this two-image sample, but no calibration study exists and no threshold is justified. They were not compared to Label Lens authority thresholds and must not be.
